title: Middle Finger Emoji 🖕 Meaning: Insult, Joke or Defiance
description: 🖕 is the obscene middle finger gesture: contempt, anger or defiance. Friends also trade it as a joke. What the emoji means and where it will get you in trouble.
summary: The 🖕 middle finger emoji is an obscene gesture meaning “f--- you.” It expresses anger, contempt or defiance toward a person, institution or situation. Among close friends it is frequently a joke, a mock insult that signals familiarity. It is the most openly rude emoji on the standard keyboard.
meaning: There is nothing subtle about it. Raising the middle finger, or “flipping the bird,” is among the oldest insulting gestures on record, mentioned by ancient Greek and Roman writers. The emoji carries the same message in text. Sent in earnest, it tells the recipient that the sender is furious with them or holds them in contempt.

Most everyday use is aimed at things rather than at the person receiving the message. People flip off Mondays, parking tickets, a rival team, a cold that will not go away. “🖕 this weather” is venting. The gesture is also a symbol of defiance in music and protest, pointed at authority, critics or an ex.

Between friends it changes into affection by insult. A buddy sends an unflattering photo of you, and you reply 🖕. Someone gloats about beating you at a game, and they get the finger. The harshness is the joke, and it only works where both people know no offense is meant. Siblings and long-time friends are the typical setting.

Unicode gives it a clinical formal name, “reversed hand with middle finger extended.” It reached phone keyboards in 2015, later than most hand gestures, and some people were surprised to see something so vulgar become official. Many platforms treat it as mature content, so it may be filtered or hidden in moderated communities and in spaces meant for children.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Meaning depends on the relationship. From a close friend after you tease them, it is banter, often followed by a laughing face. From someone you are arguing with, it is exactly as hostile as it looks and usually ends the conversation. Sent about a third party or an annoyance, it invites the recipient to share the frustration.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: It appears in defiant captions (“to everyone who doubted me 🖕”), in fan rivalries and in replies to trolls. Public posts using it against a named person can break platform rules on harassment. Musicians and comedians use it as part of a rebellious image, and its presence in a bio usually signals a blunt, unfiltered persona.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Do not use it. Even as an obvious joke between friendly colleagues, it can be screenshotted, misread or reported, and written messages are often kept as records. Employers have disciplined staff over obscene emojis in workplace chat. If you need to vent about a project, choose words and a private channel.

examples.text: You told everyone about my karaoke video?? 🖕😂
examples.meaning: A joking insult between friends; no real anger.
Genuine anger and a final dismissal.

examples.text: They said I'd never graduate. Guess what 🖕🎓
Parking ticket for being 2 minutes late 🖕🖕

examples.meaning: Sarcastic affection in reply to teasing.

combos.meaning: A playful insult; the laugh confirms it is a joke.
Double birds: emphatic contempt or frustration.
Real fury; not to be mistaken for banter.
A mocking kiss-off, mixing sweetness with insult.

confusedWith.difference: ☝️ raises the index finger with the palm forward to mean one, wait or look up. 🖕 raises the middle finger with the back of the hand outward. At tiny sizes they look alike, so check which one you have selected.
👆 also shows the back of the hand with a single finger raised, but it is the index finger, used to point at something above. Sending it by mistake for 🖕, or the reverse, is a classic typo.
🤬 shows a swearing face and conveys the sender's own rage. 🖕 directs an insult at a target. The face says “I'm furious,” and the finger says “and this is for you.”

avoid: Never use it in professional, school or customer-facing communication.
Do not send it to anyone you are not certain will take it as a joke.
Avoid posting it at specific people in public, where it can count as harassment under platform rules.
design: A fist with only the middle finger raised, shown with the back of the hand toward the viewer. Apple, Google, Samsung and Microsoft all draw it this way, with only minor differences in shading. It became available in 2015, defaults to yellow and supports skin tones.

faqs.a: It is the middle finger, an obscene insult equivalent to swearing at someone. Depending on the relationship it shows real anger or mock offense. It is also used to express frustration with a situation.

faqs.q: Is it always offensive to send 🖕?
faqs.a: No. Close friends often exchange it as teasing, and people use it to vent about things such as bad weather. It is offensive when directed seriously at a person, and it is never appropriate in formal settings.

faqs.q: What does 🖕 mean from a girl or a guy?
faqs.a: If you were joking around, it is playful, a way of saying “shut up” with a grin. If you were arguing, they are angry and probably finished talking. Emojis around it, such as a laughing face, usually show which.

faqs.q: When was the middle finger emoji added?
faqs.a: It became part of the standard emoji set in 2015, several years after gestures such as the thumbs up. Phone makers added it to their keyboards afterward, and it now appears on all major platforms.

faqs.q: Can you get in trouble for using the 🖕 emoji?
faqs.a: Yes. It can violate workplace conduct policies, school rules and social media harassment guidelines. Emojis have also been cited as evidence in legal disputes, so sending it during a conflict can count against you.
